B1.method: log10-log10 OLS on arm medians; 95% CI by run-level bootstrap (resample runs within each arm with replacement, 5,000 replicates, seed 20260716); local exponent = log(med(L2)/med(L1))/log(2) between consecutive L_long at L_short=32

neutral.corroborating_diagnostic: med T_fix / L_long^2 falls monotonically 21.6 -> 16.5 -> 13.3 -> 12.3 (finite_size_summary.neutral_law): not yet at the diffusive L^2 plateau
neutral.verdict: local exponent drifts upward toward 2 in point value (1.61 -> 1.69 -> 1.88) but the drift is not significant at n=4 geometries (trend CI spans 0). Data are consistent BOTH with a pure power law of exponent ~1.7 and with pre-asymptotic approach to the diffusive exponent 2; they do not distinguish.

loaded.verdict: no detectable curvature; local exponents 1.13, 1.17, 1.20 consistent with a single power law over 96-768

two_point_slope_Lshort128.note: consistent with zero over 192->384 at L_short=128

B1.replacement_sentence: Over the measured range L_long = 96-768 sites (L_short = 32), the median neutral fixation time scales as T_fix ∝ L_long^ζ with ζ = 1.73 (95% CI 1.60-1.90; four geometries, run-level bootstrap), and the loaded fixation time with ζ = 1.17 (1.11-1.22); their ratio, the acceleration, grows as L_long^0.56 (0.42-0.74) from 5.2 (4.4-6.2) at L_long = 96 to 16.7 (12.8-24.0) at 768. At L_short = 128 the two available lengths (192, 384) give an acceleration of 14.8 (12.2-17.6) and 15.7 (13.4-23.5).
B1.not_established: Nothing beyond L_long = 768 is measured. The neutral exponent is a two-decade-short apparent exponent: its running value rises from 1.61 (96-192) to 1.88 (384-768) toward the diffusive value 2 - a drift the four geometries cannot yet distinguish from zero (trend +0.14 per octave, CI -0.13 to +0.47), so the neutral law, and with it the acceleration exponent, must not be extrapolated to tissue scale; if the neutral arm reaches ζ = 2 asymptotically the asymptotic acceleration exponent would be ~0.8, not 0.57.

B2.data: six per-geometry sigma_DeltaR values with 95% CIs (finite_size_summary.gap_process.sigma_dR_per_frame); N = clone area = L_long*L_short/2. Per-run gap series are not persisted in the store, so the comparison is on the six geometry values with parametric CI propagation (20,000 lognormal resamples within each geometry's CI).

isotropic_N_model_eta_fixed_half.note: visually indistinguishable from the free-eta fit (eta=0.503)

comparison.caveat: n = 6 geometries; AICc penalises the 3-parameter model heavily at this n (AICc iso +0.48 vs ani +15.4) - the decisive evidence is the controlled same-area pair, not the information criterion

B2.winner: anisotropic (L_long^-0.74 L_short^-0.26). The isotropic exponent eta = 0.50 [0.46, 0.55] is a real feature of the pooled fit but the isotropic model is falsified by the equal-area pair: 192x128 and 768x32 both have N = 12,288 yet sigma_DeltaR differs 1.93x with non-overlapping CIs.
B2.replacement_sentence: The per-run scatter of the ratchet-rate difference decays with domain size, but not with clone area alone: fitting the six geometries gives σ_ΔR ∝ L_long^-0.74 (0.68-0.80) L_short^-0.26 (0.20-0.32), and two geometries of equal clone area (192x128 vs 768x32, N = 12,288) differ 1.93-fold (non-overlapping CIs), which the naive central-limit form σ_ΔR ∝ N^-1/2 forbids. The exponents sum to 1.00 (0.91-1.09), so σ_ΔR is intensive in the total area only up to this anisotropy. [State as an empirical fit; the six geometries are not a factorial design, so p and q are partially confounded and no mechanism is claimed.]
B2.not_established: The mechanistic origin of the anisotropy (weight -0.74 along the interface-crossing direction vs -0.26 across it). The six geometries do not form a factorial grid (L_long spans 8x, L_short 4x, only two shared columns), so the exponent pair is a description of these six points, not a validated law; the pooled N^-0.50 [0.46, 0.55] fit should be reported only as the leading term with a 1.5x worst-case residual.

genuine_out_of_sample.absolute_scale: the same prediction under-shoots the loaded median T_fix by a factor 0.52-0.62 at every L_short (loaded_pred_over_lattice in reduced_model_summary), i.e. it gets the exponent, not the prefactor
genuine_out_of_sample.collapse_LOO: a partial internal check only: predicting each geometry's median from the other five via the shared C gives relative errors -8.5% to +14.6% (still uses beta and sigma from the target geometry's own runs)

B3.honest_description: A one-constant scaling collapse: with the front-response coefficient β and the rate-scatter σ_ΔR both measured from the loaded fixation ensemble itself, a single fitted constant C = 1.64 ± 0.11 (CV 6.8%) places all six geometries on T_fix = C sqrt(L_long/(β σ_ΔR)); this demonstrates internal consistency of the ballistic-sweep form, not a parameter-free prediction. The genuinely out-of-sample test is the reduced model: with D_g, v(g) and D_0 measured in three separate ensembles (none containing the L_short-scan fixation runs), the simulated SDE predicts a loaded exponent of 0.150 in L_short against 0.173 [0.125, 0.213] measured, while under-predicting the absolute scale by ~0.6x and failing on the neutral exponent (0.94 predicted vs 0.66 measured).
B3.not_established: Any claim of a 'parameter-free' or 'no fitted parameter' collapse. C is fitted; beta and sigma_DeltaR are same-ensemble inputs. Also unestablished: absolute-scale predictivity of the reduced model (systematically ~0.6x) and its neutral-arm exponent.
